source: 1-loop box (s=100, t=-1) with D0 = 7/3 instead of the default 4.  Same target as box1_single_solve_integrals_mma.wl (j[box1, 1, 0, 1, 0]) but exercises GlobalOptions::d0: SolveIntegrals samples at the internal eps grid epslist0 + (4-D0)/2 (AMFlow.m:1342, 1351) and FitEps fits the Laurent expansion against the user-facing grid (AMFlow.m:1356).  First end-to-end Milestone 3 D0 != 4 parity check.

cpp_status.result: C++ Laurent expansion at D0 = 7/3 matches MMA across orders 0, 1, 2 to ~30 significant digits.  C++ leading_order = 0 (1-loop trim from fit_leading_order = -2 to actual_leading = 0); MMA leading is also 0 after Series + N truncation to epsorder + leading = 4 + (-2) = 2.  Both sides expose 3 user-facing coefficients (orders 0..2).

max_absolute_difference.comment: Compared C++ acb_t midpoint vs MMA value rounded to 30 sig digits.  MMA working_pre = 182 (~54.7 dec) so its 30-digit rounding is exact at this scale; C++ acb_t error balls (~1e-30 to 4e-32, see acb output) bracket the MMA value in every coefficient.
